full_judgment:
Shahabuddin Ahmed, J:-The question involved in this appeal by special leave is whether the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division was well founded in lay in refusing to stay the further proceedings of a suit under section 34 of the Arbitration Act, 1940. The suit itself was instituted under section 20 of the Arbitration Act for filing an arbitration agreement in Court since a dispute arose between the parties about the subject matter of the suit which was also covered by the Arbitration Clause of a Contract between the parties. The trial court stayed the proceedings, but in revision the learned Single Judge held that the provision for stay of the proceedings of a suit as laid down in section 34 of the Arbitration Act would not apply to this case. 

 (2) The application shall be in writing and shall be numbered and registered as a miscellaneous case between one or more of the parties interested or claiming to be interested as applicant or applicants and remainder as opposite party or opposite parties, if the application has been presented by all the parties or if otherwise, between the applicant and other parties. 

 (2A) A miscellaneous case registered under sub-section (2) shall, unless the Court considers it necessary to take any other evidence, ordinarily be disposed of on affidavit. 

 4. Section 34 is attracted to a case in which a party to an arbitration agreement files a suit for resolution of a dispute ignoring his own agreement that the matter shall be resolved by an arbitrator and not by a Court. This section comes into play when such a party to the agreement tries to avoid reference of the dispute to the arbitrator. In such a case, the Court, if moved in time, may stop proceedings of such a suit and. direct that the matter be settled by an arbitrator in terms of the agreement. Section 20, on the other hand, comes in aid of the party who intends to submit the dispute to an arbitrator in terms of the agreement, but who has failed to do so because of unwillingness or lack of response of the other party to the agreement to refer the dispute to the arbitrator. Stay of proceedings of the suit filed under this section is not therefore, contemplated in section 34 the ultimate purpose of both, the section being the same-reference of the dispute, which is the subject-matter of an arbitration agreement to the arbitrator. The learned Single Judge is found to have correctly construed these provisions of law 

 5. Defendant-appellant, is trying to invoke the provision of s.34 for stay of the proceedings of the suit contending that the subject- matter of the suit being the same as the subject-matter of the arbitration agreement, this should be referred to the arbitrator in terms of the arbitration clause 7 of the Contract. The plaintiff-respondent is also seeking practically the same remedy by instituting the suit under section 20, that is to say, for a direction that the arbitration agreement be filed in the Court so that the dispute can be referred to the arbitrator. As such there should not have been any resistance from the defendant to the institution of the suit under section 20 if the defendant sincerely desires that the dispute should be settled by arbitration. Similarly, the plaintiff should have no objection to die dispute being submitted to the arbitrator. But the conflict of interest of the parties will reveal itself if their respective contentions are looked into. Both the parties to the agreement are apparently willing that the dispute be settled by arbitration as provided in clause 7 of their Contract. But, according to the arbitration agreement, Secretary of the Ministry of Commerce will nominate the arbitrator the plaintiff it appears, apprehends that the Secretary of the Ministry concerned may not take an impartial view of the matter, and, for that reason, the plaintiff is trying to make out a case for appointment of a new arbitrator in place of the Secretary. It is to be seen whether the Court is empowered under section 20 to replace an arbitrator about whose appointment the parties to the arbitration agreement has already agreed. Function of the Court under this section is that when, after hearing the parties the Court is satisfied that the dispute covered by the arbitration agreement should be referred to the arbitrator, then the Court shall refer the dispute to the arbitrator "appointed by the parties", whether in the agreement or otherwise, and where the parties cannot agree upon an arbitrator, to an arbitrator appointed by it. Thereafter, the arbitration shall proceed in accordance with law. In this case, both the parties agreed as per the Arbitration Clause that the Secretary of the Ministry would nominate the arbitrator. If the Court is satisfied that the arbitration-agreement should be filed then the Court will refer the dispute to the arbitrator to be nominated by the Secretary of the Ministry. Question of change of the arbitrator is not relevant when the parties agreed upon his appointment in the Agreement.
